reviews.title: Not Your Typical Show
reviews.body: Frantically, I got off work late and 30 miles away I broke every law in book to weedle my way through stalled-ox traffic to get to the show. San Francisco was still amidst a protracted Indian summer and it was remarkably warm for their city. I did not carry a jacket. Walking into Winterland I noticed that there was not the usual melee' in the street or on the sidewalk fronting the venue. Security guard paid me no mind as I strolled quizzically through the doors. They ignored me. I didn't even present my ticket. I walked straight into the main floor and essentially right on up to the front of the stage. It was not at all crowded. I wondered why. What was going on? Was there a bomb scare, or something? Without hoopla or introduction Weir, Lesh and Garcia quickly came out, tuned up and launched into it. Also should note: This one I attended clean -- no drugs, no booze. Head up at 7, the Dead started. They played wonderfully throughout. Though it fails me, I cannot recall anything special about the night's music. Funny, I only recall that there was a slight anomaly in my ears to the drums. As I listen to this recording now I can hear it, but it does not spoil the overall effect. Thank you, Jay Ashley. This is, every note, a magnificent show. Thank you Archives.

reviews.title: Hits Different
reviews.body: This show really stands on it's own. It is the most ''acoustic'' electric show ! have heard from '74. The sound is super intimate and i love it. Vocals WAY out front. I don't know if it's because of the double mics or what but, it's beautiful and i'm all here for it. My 2nd favorite Dew besides the '72 Stanley Theater. Great BEW. This is not to be missed. All around great performance and recording. I cannot even describe how much joy it brings me to be able to sit here and listen to these shows, thanks Archive.... thanks Jay

reviews.title: A Gem
reviews.body: The whole show is tip top, and even Donna is on, but the jam->Dark Star->Dew is one for the ages. It's not a spacy, indulgent Dark Star, but a seemingly well-crafted musical Dark Star, with very smooth transitions, and a mellow feel throughout. At one point it evolves into a funky feel reminiscent of jazz-rock of the same period. (There are other instances of this in 1973-1974 as well.) And yes, another great Dew in a great Dew year. From Not Fade Away until the end is spot-on, clean, tight Dead rock and roll.

reviews.title: best Dew I’ve heard
reviews.body: Wow, this show is amazing. The entire first set is perfect as well as the second set. The jam into Dark Star is genius and the Dark Star itself is very good. It’s nice and mellow, not too spacey, and even gets pretty funky for a bit. But the Morning Dew is what makes this show so special. It’s filled with energy and emotion and the solo sections are absolutely nuts. This is THE Dew. Check it out asap.

reviews.title: Dew
reviews.body: One of the strongest shows of '74, and the second set is one of most unique sets ever. As stated earlier, a complete meltdown, and the best Morning Dew of the year in an incredible Dew year (2/24,3/23,6/18,9/10). Yes it's the one in the the movie, and for my ears, perhaps the best all-time performance - totally tight, zero mistakes, huge power from Phil, incredible dynamics, perfect!
